title: Texas Branch Legal Note: Owner's Statutory Retention on Overdue Reconstruction Draws
content:
The owner's statutory retention is set against the balance an overdue draw charge on a Reconstruction contract is figured on, because a retained amount is not past due.

**The Texas retention.** For a property whose loss address is in Texas, the owner retains part of the contract price until the Texas statutory retention days after the work is completed (Texas Property Code, Chapter 53); the company's rules take that retention as the Texas owner retention percentage of the contract price, 10%, for 30 days, which the owner holds back itself from its own payments of the customer-funded draws, while the final draw holds it back on the share of the contract the customer does not fund.

**Set against the balance.** For a Texas property, until 30 days after the substantial completion date have passed:

- on a tier that withholds no retainage, 10% of the draw's requested amount is set against the balance;
- on a tier that withholds retainage, the part of the 10% above the tier's retainage percentage, of the draw's requested amount.

For every other property nothing is set against it.

**Paid in full.** For a property whose loss address is in Texas, until 30 days after the substantial completion date have passed, a customer-funded draw counts as paid in full once everything but its statutory retention is paid; its statutory retention is 10% of its requested amount, on a tier that withholds retainage the part of that percentage above the tier's retainage percentage.

## By agreement

| Agreement | Tier retainage | Share of the draw's requested amount set against the balance (Texas, within the period) |
|---|---|---|
| Repair Agreement - Minor Repairs | 0% | 10% |
| Standard Rebuild Agreement | 0% | 10% |
| Major Rebuild Agreement | 0% | 10% |
| Full Structural Rebuild Agreement | 5% | 5% |
| Multifamily Unit Rebuild Agreement | 0% | 10% |
| Commercial Interior Rebuild Agreement | 10% | 0% |

## The period

The period runs while the contract has no substantial completion date, and after it up to and including the 30th day after the substantial completion date (days counted as calendar days, the completion date itself not counted). On the 31st day the retention is no longer set against the balance.

**Example (hypothetical).** A Texas customer-funded draw requested at $7,000.00 on an agreement that withholds no retainage, 12 days after substantial completion: $700.00 is set against the balance; if everything but $700.00 has been paid, the draw counts as paid in full.
